alerts.title: Parasympathetic Autonomic Attenuation
alerts.reason: Post-EVA recovery latency and sleep deficit below 6.5 hours triggered autonomic fatigue flag.
alerts.suggestedAction: Prescribe 10-minute guided resonant breathing (0.1 Hz); adjust scheduled EVA timeline.
alerts.dismissalReason: Verified transient post-ARED recovery lag; seated trace nominal.

researchReferences.title: The NASA Twins Study: A multidimensional analysis of a year-long human spaceflight
researchReferences.authors: Garrett-Bakelman, F. E., Darshi, M., Green, S. J., et al.
researchReferences.studyPopulation: 1 astronaut (340 days on ISS) paired with identical twin control on Earth
researchReferences.summary: Identified transient telomere elongation, vascular wall remodeling, and sustained immune pathway activation during long-duration flight.
keyFindings: Post-flight cardiovascular deceleration rate exhibits transient attenuation.
91.3% of expression changes returned to pre-flight baselines within six months of recovery.
researchReferences.methodology: Longitudinal genomics, physiological telemetry, multi-omics profiling
researchReferences.knownLimitations: Single identical twin pair study limits broad statistical generalizability.

researchReferences.title: Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced changes in bone mineral density
researchReferences.authors: Sibonga, J. D., Evans, H. J., Sung, H. G., et al.
researchReferences.source: NASA Human Research Program Human Research Roadmap
researchReferences.studyPopulation: ISS crew members participating in ARED and CEVIS countermeasure protocols
researchReferences.summary: Axial mechanical loading via Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) successfully limits bone mineral density loss to under 1.0% per month.
keyFindings: Unmitigated microgravity produces 1.0% to 1.5% monthly trabecular bone loss.
ARED countermeasure combined with Vitamin D3 preserves proximal femur geometry.
researchReferences.methodology: Longitudinal pre- and post-flight DXA imaging and in-flight biochemical markers
researchReferences.knownLimitations: Micro-CT resolution unavailable in-flight; relies on post-landing scans.

researchReferences.title: Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration spaceflight
researchReferences.authors: Stahn, A. C., Werner, A., Opatz, O., et al.
researchReferences.studyPopulation: 11 astronauts performing cycle ergometry aboard the ISS
researchReferences.summary: Demonstrated chronic elevation of astronaut core body temperature by ~1.0°C during rest and exercise due to impaired evaporative convection.
keyFindings: Core body temperature shifts upward by ~1.0°C under weightlessness.
Elevated IL-6 levels suggest a sustained low-grade systemic inflammatory response.
researchReferences.methodology: Non-invasive double-sensor forehead heat flux thermometry
researchReferences.knownLimitations: Conducted under microgravity forced-air ventilation constraints.
